title: Who leads the Bs?
hook: Two correct sorts of one list can disagree about who comes first among equals.

knows: sorting a hand by sliding cards left (insertion-by-hand)
doesNotKnow: that two sorting methods can give different results when items tie

misconception: Sorted is sorted: any correct sort of the same list gives the same list.
objective: The learner can explain that a stable sort never lets equal items pass each other, so sorting by one key keeps the order of the previous key, while a swap-based selection sort can reorder ties.

claims.text: Sorting Ana (B), Ben (A), Cal (B), Dee (A) by grade, A before B, by sliding each card left past higher grades gives Ben, Dee, Ana, Cal; swapping the first smallest grade to the front gives Ben, Dee, Cal, Ana.
claims.source: Builder's node script (insertion with strict 'higher grade' test; selection with strict less-than, first minimum, swap into front). Insertion rows: Ben Ana Cal Dee / Ben Ana Cal Dee / Ben Dee Ana Cal. Selection rows: Ben Ana Cal Dee / Ben Dee Cal Ana / Ben Dee Cal Ana. Matches the designer's re-run in company/design/specs/ties-keep-their-order.md. Reference only: TheAlgorithms/Python sorts/insertion_sort.py, selection_sort.py.

claims.text: On swap 2, swapping Dee with Ana throws Ana past Cal, which has the same grade; Cal stays put on slide step 2 because Ana is not a higher grade.
claims.source: Rows above: before swap 2 the order is Ben Ana Cal Dee; swapping slot 2 (Ana) with slot 4 (Dee) gives Ben Dee Cal Ana, so Ana moves from before Cal to after it. Slide step 2: Cal's left neighbour Ana has grade B, not higher than B, so Cal does not move.

claims.text: A sort that never lets equal items pass each other is called stable. Insertion sort (sliding past strictly higher items only) is stable; selection sort done with swaps is not.
claims.source: CLRS 3rd ed. section 8.2 (definition of stable) and 2.1 (insertion sort); the unstable example for selection sort is the swap-2 run in c1/c2. · Fact-check 2026-10-14 (pass 19): CLRS 4th ed. uses the same numbering (stable defined in 8.2, insertion sort in 2.1).

claims.text: Sorting a spreadsheet by name and then (stably) by grade keeps names in order inside each grade.
claims.source: After the name sort, equal-grade rows are in name order; a stable grade sort never reorders equal grades, so they stay in name order. Requires the grade sort to be stable (spreadsheet tools differ).

recall.question: A list is sorted by name. You then sort it by grade with a stable sort. Two students have the same grade. Which comes first?
options: The one earlier in the alphabet
The one later in the alphabet
recall.why: A stable sort never lets equal items pass each other, so students with the same grade keep their name order.
